# How review pages are built

Every card set review has its own page at `/reviews/<slug>/` (for
example `/reviews/1991-92-mcdonalds-all-stars/`). Those pages are
**generated by every Amplify build** and **a CMS save starts a build**,
so adding or editing a set needs no manual step. This document explains
how that works, why it was built this way, and where it stops short of
a full static-site setup. Written 2026-10-30; the change log at the end
records how it got here.

## The short version

- The review pages are not in git. Each Amplify build runs
  `tools/generateReviewPages/generate.mjs`, which reads the live card
  sets from the public API and writes the pages, a link manifest
  (`reviews/index.json`) and `sitemap.xml` into the build output.
- A save to a live set in the CMS writes to the `Cards` table. A
  DynamoDB Stream on that table calls the `cardsRebuildTrigger` Lambda,
  which starts an Amplify build. About three minutes later the new page
  is live.
- The generated page is the old `waxReviews.html` with its `<head>`, its
  few global variables and, since 2026-11-19, the review itself filled in
  for one set: the set details, the review text, the images, the category
  intro, the breadcrumbs and both JSON-LD blocks are in the HTML (see
  "The review, pre-rendered"). `wax.js` still fetches the set and redraws
  the same markup, adding pagination and votes; the checklist modal and
  the ticker stay browser-only.
- Each set with a checklist also gets its own page,
  `/reviews/<slug>/checklist/`, with the full list in the HTML (see
  "Checklist pages").
- Old query-string URLs (`waxReviews.html?year=1991&...`) keep working.
- Since 2026-11-05 the generator also pre-renders the shared blocks
  whose links point at review pages: the nav and footer (every public
  page and review page), the year picker (every review page) and the
  Browse By Set columns, with final `/reviews/<slug>/` links in the HTML
  (see "Links" below).
- The same build then minifies the public scripts and `styles.css` in
  place (see "The rest of the build: minified assets"); the repo keeps the
  readable source.

## The pipeline

```
CMS save (createCardPost / updateCardSet / delete; saveChecklist stamps the set too)
        |
        v
DynamoDB Cards table --- stream (new + old images)
        |  batch window 60 s
        v
Lambda cardsRebuildTrigger --- amplify:StartJob (RELEASE, branch main)
        |
        v
Amplify build (amplify.yml)
   npm ci                                    (installs esbuild only)
   node tools/generateReviewPages/generate.mjs
        reads getPublicCardSets (live sets, stars, SEO fields)
              getCardSetsByYear (each year's full records: review text, details)
              getChecklistBySetName (each set's checklist)
        templates: waxReviews.html, tools/generateReviewPages/checklistTemplate.html
        writes: reviews/<slug>/index.html           (one per set, review pre-rendered)
                reviews/<slug>/checklist/index.html (one per set with a checklist)
                reviews/index.json                  (link manifest)
                sitemap.xml
        fills in place: the nav and footer of 8 static pages,
                        browseBySet.html's two columns
   node tools/minifyAssets/minify.mjs        (public JS + styles.css, in place)
   rm -rf node_modules                       (keep it out of the artifact)
   rm -rf "Old HTML Pages"                   (archived pages aren't published)
        |
        v
Deploy to Amplify Hosting (CloudFront) --- amplifyBuildNotifier emails the result
```

A `git push` to `main` starts the same build, so code changes and
content changes share one path.

1. **CMS save.** `createCardPost` and `updateCardSet` check the SEO
   Friendly URL (see "URL design"), then write to `Cards`.
2. **Stream and trigger.** The stream carries both the old and the new
   copy of the item. `Lambdas/cardsRebuildTrigger/` compares them and
   only acts when something that reaches the output changed on a set
   that is, or was, live (`blogStatus` "OK"): `blogStatus`, `setName`,
   `year`, `blogCat`, `setID`, `stars`, the SEO fields, the header
   image, `now` and `updatedAt`, and since 2026-11-19 everything the
   pre-rendered review shows (`postBody`, `size`, `subsets`, `formats`,
   `mfg`, `author`, the footer image, `printRun`), `hasChecklist` and
   `checklistUpdatedAt`. Only vote counts don't start a build, because
   the page's own JavaScript shows them live. Every CMS save moves
   `updatedAt`, so every CMS save does start one; that is deliberate, it
   keeps the sitemap's `<lastmod>` honest. A checklist save or delete
   (`saveChecklist`) writes `checklistUpdatedAt` on the set's `Cards`
   item, so it starts one too, which rebuilds that checklist page. A
   burst of saves inside the 60 second batch window becomes one build.
3. **Build.** `amplify.yml` runs `npm ci`, then the generator, then the
   asset minifier (see "The rest of the build: minified assets"), then
   deletes `node_modules`, all before the artifact is zipped. The build
   image is Amazon Linux 2 with Node 16.19 (read from a diagnostic build's
   log), which has no global `fetch`, so the generator uses `node:https`
   and retries three times. Git history is complete, so the static pages'
   `<lastmod>` (their last commit date) works.
4. **Generator.** It fetches each year's full set records (37 requests,
   four at a time) and each checklist (64, two at a time); the whole run
   takes about 15 seconds. For each live set it takes `waxReviews.html`
   as a template, replaces two marked blocks (below) and fills the rest
   (nav, footer, year picker, breadcrumbs, intro, the review), then
   writes the page, and writes the set's checklist page from
   `checklistTemplate.html`. It also writes the manifest and the sitemap,
   and fills the nav and footer markers of the static pages and the
   Browse By Set columns in the build's copy.
5. **Deploy and notify.** Amplify deploys the artifact. The existing
   `amplifyBuildNotifier` emails the result, including the failing
   step's log link if the build failed.

## What the generator checks

Nothing is written unless every live set passes:

- a `seoURLSlug` that is present, lowercase letters, numbers and single
  hyphens, and unique among live sets;
- every marker pair found exactly once: `review-head`, `review-params`,
  `set-picker`, `breadcrumbs`, `card-intro`, `review-body`, `nav` and
  `footer` in `waxReviews.html`; `checklist-head`, `breadcrumbs`, `nav`
  and `footer` (plus its `__TOKEN__` placeholders) in
  `checklistTemplate.html`; `nav` and `footer` in each static page, which
  must also name a known `NAV_MAP` key in `data-nav-page`;
  `browse-major` and `browse-fastfood` in `browseBySet.html`;
- the browser functions it runs (below) found and loadable: the
  `nav-block` and `footer-block` slices of `helper.js` and the
  `checklist-block` slice of `wax.js`, `setPickerHtml`,
  `buildCardSetMarkup`, `cardSetJsonLd`, `cardIntroHtml` and friends, and
  `browseColumnHtml` in `browseBySet.js`;
- every checklist loaded (`CHECKLIST_API_URL`, read from `wax.js`): the
  review pages and Browse By Set link to every checklist page, so a
  checklist that still fails after three tries fails the build rather
  than ship a link to a missing page;
- `stars` present in the API response (otherwise `getPublicCardSets` has
  not been redeployed with it);
- `categoryRanges` readable from `scripts/helper.js`, and a range that
  covers each set's year (that is where each set's `pageName` comes
  from, so a new season only needs `helper.js` extended).

Warnings, not errors: a missing meta description (the page gets a
generic one); a year whose full records still fail to load (its pages
are written without the pre-rendered review, as before 2026-11-19, and
the browser draws it); and a set flagged `hasChecklist` whose checklist
comes back empty (its checklist page shows the "No checklist data" text,
is `noindex` and stays out of the sitemap). The one year-and-category
combination with no review
(2004-05 McDonald's, the lockout season) is skipped.

If any check fails the generator exits non-zero, the **build fails**,
Amplify **keeps the previous deployment live**, and the notifier emails
the log. The site never ends up half-generated.

## `waxReviews.html`: before and now

**Before:** one file served every review, at
`waxReviews.html?year=1991&pageName=mcd&blogCat=mcd` (plus `&setID=` in
a multi-set year). An inline script read those four values from the
query string, `wax.js` fetched the year's sets from the API and drew
the shown one, and `fetchPageTitle()` replaced the generic `<head>` with
the set's title, description, social tags and canonical once the data
arrived. The nav, year picker and Player Search linked to query-string
URLs.

**Now, it does two jobs:**

1. **It is the template.** Two pairs of marker comments wrap the parts
   the generator swaps: `review-head` (title, description, social tags)
   and `review-params` (the script that defines `year`, `sortOrder`,
   `pageName`, `blogCat` and `setID`). In a generated page the head has
   that set's real title, description, canonical, `og:*` and
   `twitter:*` tags, and the globals are fixed values. The inline
   `DOMContentLoaded` handler now reads the global `setID` instead of
   `params.get("setID")`; that one change is what let the generator fix
   the value. The masthead and checklist-modal links went from
   `index.html` to `/index.html`, because a page now sits one folder
   deeper, and on 2026-11-10 to `/`, so Home shows as the bare domain.
2. **It still serves old URLs.** Served as-is, with its generic head and
   globals read from the query string. When the set loads, JavaScript
   sets the metadata and replaces the address bar with
   `/reviews/<slug>/`, and the canonical points at that page. Bookmarks
   and shared links keep working, and search engines consolidate them
   onto the slug page without any redirect rules.

What a generated page does when opened: the head, globals, intro, year
picker, breadcrumbs and review are already in the HTML; the same scripts
run; `fetchCardSetsByYear` loads the year (no spinner, since the review
is already showing) and redraws the set whose `setID` matches, with the
pagination and vote buttons; `fetchPageTitle` writes the breadcrumbs and
structured data again but leaves the build's title and tags alone (see
"Titles"); on `window.load` the nav, footer
and masthead render and the links are upgraded (below).

## Loading speed: what a generated head preloads

On a phone the page's largest element is the set's header image. Until
2026-11-19 its `<img>` only existed once `wax.js` had downloaded, run,
fetched the year's data and drawn the set; it is now in the pre-rendered
HTML, but the preloads below still start both downloads from the
`<head>`, before the browser reaches the body. The generator puts them in
each generated head (`headBlock()` in `generate.mjs`):

- **The header image**, a high-priority image preload of the set's
  `headerImg` + `headerImgName` (the same URL `buildCardSetMarkup()` uses,
  so the preload and the later `<img>` match). A set with no header image
  gets none.
- **The set data**, a `preload` of kind `fetch` (with `crossorigin`) for
  `https://a92dwyl3ic.execute-api.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/dev?year=&blogCat=`
  with that page's values. `fetchCardSetsByYear()` in `wax.js` calls the
  identical URL with a plain `fetch()`, which the browser answers from the
  preload, so the request starts about a second earlier on a slow phone
  and is still sent only once (checked). The URL lives in two places, the
  `SETS_BY_YEAR_URL` constant in `generate.mjs` and `wax.js`; if they ever
  differ the preload is just wasted and the page still works, but the
  speed-up is lost.

A header image uploaded since the CMS's image processing (an
`img/cards/v2/` file) has a phone copy, `<name>-sm.webp`: the header
preload is then two media-scoped preloads, one per device, matching the
`<picture>` that `buildCardSetMarkup()` writes (`phoneImageUrl()` in
`helper.js`, run by the generator too), so a phone never downloads the
large file. Two related details: the API preconnect in the template has
`crossorigin`, because CORS fetches use a different connection pool from
credentialed ones; and the old inline script that preloaded a
`<year>_hero.webp` file was removed, since the page never used that file
(for some sets the header image *is* the hero file, and those now get it
through the header preload).

Old query-string URLs get neither preload: the template doesn't know the
year until JavaScript reads the address, and those pages replace their
address with the slug URL anyway.

## Links: pre-rendered by the build, upgraded in the browser

**Why pre-render (2026-11-05).** Search Console listed 45 old
`waxReviews.html?...` URLs as "Duplicate without user-selected
canonical" and none of the slug pages crawled. Every link to a slug page
was drawn by JavaScript with a query-string `href` first, so a crawler
reading the raw HTML only ever found the old URLs (which all share one
raw HTML with no canonical), and a rendered snapshot could catch them
before the upgrade.

**How.** The nav, footer, year picker and Browse By Set columns are each
built by one pure function in the browser code (`navHtml()`,
`footerHtml()`, `setPickerHtml()` in `helper.js`; `browseColumnHtml()` in
`browseBySet.js`). The generator runs those same functions at build time
in a `node:vm` sandbox: it lifts the `// nav-block:start`/`:end` and
`// footer-block:start`/`:end` slices of `helper.js`, a few single
functions by name (`escapeHtml`, `getPageNameForYear`, `setPickerHtml`,
`compareSetsForDefault`, `reviewLinkAttrs`, and `stripYearFromSetName`
from `wax.js`; the review's own functions are listed under "The review,
pre-rendered"), and all of `browseBySet.js`. It passes each function an
`hrefFor` resolver that returns a link's final `/reviews/<slug>/` URL
(the year's default set, by `compareSetsForDefault()`, exactly what
`applyReviewLinks()` would pick), and writes the result between marker
comments, keeping the markers. One implementation serves both places,
so the pre-rendered markup can't drift from what the browser would draw;
it was checked to be identical on all 71 pages. The browser code skips a
block that is already present (`fetchNav()`, `fetchFooterLinks()`,
`renderSetPicker()`), so there's no query-then-slug flicker. A year with
no live set (2004 McDonald's) keeps its query link, which redirects to
`lockout.html`.

The static pages are tracked files, so a local generator run leaves them
modified: discard those changes (in Amplify it only touches the build's
copy).

**In the browser.** Old query-string pages (`waxReviews.html?...`) and
the breadcrumb and Player Search results still use the original path:
they render with the query-string `href` plus `data-review-cat` /
`data-review-year` (or `data-review-setid`) attributes. `helper.js`
starts loading `/reviews/index.json` as soon as it runs, and
`applyReviewLinks()` swaps in `/reviews/<slug>/` for every such link
once it arrives.

The manifest is written by the same build as the pages, so it only ever
lists pages that exist in that deployment: no window where a link
points at a page that has not been built yet, no per-page API call, and
no way to drift from the pages. If it has not loaded, or a set is not in
it, the query link stays and still works (the page then rewrites its own
address). The CMS pages never load it.

A year's default set (the one a bare-year link opens) is the highest
rated, ties broken by set name A to Z. `compareSetsForDefault()` in
`helper.js` is that rule, and `wax.js` sorts a year's sets with the same
function, so the year links and the old bare-year URLs agree. (Before
2026-10-30 ties followed DynamoDB's order, which is arbitrary.)

## The review, pre-rendered

**Why (2026-11-19).** The raw HTML of a review page held only its head,
H1 and links: the 600 to 1,500-word review, the set details, the images,
the breadcrumbs and the structured data all came from the API through
`wax.js`. Google reads that only in a later, lower-priority rendering
pass, and Bing, AI crawlers and link previews mostly don't run
JavaScript, so to them each review was empty.

**How.** The same way as the links: the generator runs the browser's own
functions in its sandbox, with each set's full record. The public list
doesn't carry the review text, so `fetchFullSets()` requests the
year-by-category endpoint the page itself uses (`SETS_BY_YEAR_URL`, so
the records are identical), once per year and category, four at a time.
Into `waxReviews.html`'s markers it writes:

- `review-body` (inside `#cardSetDiv`): `buildCardSetMarkup()` with the
  same fields `displayCardSet()` passes, including the Checklist link's
  `href` (the set's checklist page);
- `card-intro`: `cardIntroHtml(pageName)` (`wax.js`), the category intro
  ("Classic '80s Sets..."), which also stops the page jumping when it
  used to arrive after the first paint;
- `breadcrumbs`: `breadcrumbTrail()` and `breadcrumbHtml()` (`helper.js`),
  with the category link already resolved to its `/reviews/` page;
- in `review-head`, both JSON-LD blocks, `jsonld-cardset`
  (`cardSetJsonLd()`, `wax.js`) and `jsonld-breadcrumbs`
  (`breadcrumbJsonLd()`), with the ids `setJsonLd()` replaces, so the
  browser never duplicates them.

The hidden crawler-only `#pageHeader` H1 is dropped when the review is
pre-rendered (the set name in the set details is the page's one H1), and
still filled for a page whose year failed to load. The small wrapped
logos in a review (`.img-wrap-sm`/`.img-wrap-md`) get their phone size
in the markup itself (`withWrapSizes()`, run by `buildCardSetMarkup()`),
where it used to be set by script after the review rendered, so they are
the right size from the first paint.

**In the browser.** `wax.js` still fetches the year and redraws the set:
the redraw is identical (checked on all three test pages), happens in
the same frame, and adds the pagination and vote buttons below, so
votes and fresh content keep working. A pre-rendered page shows no
loading spinner, and a failed or empty reply leaves the pre-rendered
review in place instead of the error text. Layout shift measured 0 to
0.001 on desktop.

Dates: `fixDate()` formats the byline in the build's time zone (UTC), so
a review published late in the evening (Eastern) shows the next day in
the raw HTML; a visitor sees their local date after the redraw.

## Checklist pages

**Why (2026-11-19).** "<set> checklist" is one of the commonest
collector searches, but every checklist lived only in the modal, which
loads after a click. Each set with a checklist now has a page at
`/reviews/<slug>/checklist/`, titled "<set> Hockey Card Checklist (N Cards)", with
a description built from the data ("all 759 cards, including 1 insert
set, with rookie cards marked"), its canonical, social tags, breadcrumbs
(Home, category, the review, Checklist) and their JSON-LD.

**How.** `fetchChecklists()` loads each set's checklist from
`getChecklistBySetName` (two requests at a time, for the `Checklists`
table's throughput cap). `buildChecklistPage()` fills
`tools/generateReviewPages/checklistTemplate.html` (a `noindex` page
when unfilled): the list is `renderChecklistGroups()`, lifted with the
rest of the modal's rendering code from the `// checklist-block` slice
of `wax.js`, and `checklistFilterAvailability()` decides which filter
checkboxes show. The page is the modal's own parts laid out as a page
(`.checklist-page-panel`): Print, Download PDF, the Inserts / Rookies
filters, the list and the print-only masthead and footer. The filters
and Download PDF start disabled; `initChecklistPage()` (`wax.js`) loads
the cards they work from, redraws the identical list and turns them on.
Printing a checklist page prints only the list, as the modal does.

**Links.** On a review page the Checklist link's `href` is the checklist
page, so crawlers follow it, but a click still opens the modal. Browse
By Set links straight to the checklist pages. Every checklist URL is in
the sitemap; its `<lastmod>` is the later of the set's date and its last
checklist save (`checklistUpdatedAt`).

## Titles

**Why (2026-11-19).** The title is what a searcher sees and clicks in
the results. Every review was "<set> Hockey Card Set Review", which says
nothing about what the page offers.

**How.** A review's title is `reviewPageTitle()` (`helper.js`), run by the generator with
the set's checklist (fetched before the review pages are built, for
this): "<set> Hockey Card Review: Key Rookies & Checklist" when the main
set has RC cards (the rule the modal's Rookies filter uses,
`checklistFilterAvailability()`), "<set> Hockey Card Review & Checklist"
when it has none (most fast-food sets), "<set> Hockey Card Review" with
no checklist. So it never promises something a set lacks. The same
value goes into `<title>`, `og:title` and `twitter:title`. The set name
comes first because Google shows about 60 characters; longer names lose
the tail. In the browser, `fetchPageTitle()` leaves a generated page's
head alone, since it can't see the checklist; an old query-string URL
gets the template without the rookies part. Checklist pages are "<set>
Hockey Card Checklist (N Cards)".

The CMS has no SEO Title field (see `CMS_GUIDE.md`): every save sends
it blank. The 64 titles stored before this were cleared once, so every
set uses the template. The generator still honours a non-blank
`seoPageTitle`, so an override field could come back without data work.

## URL design

- **Slug.** The existing `seoURLSlug` field, now required in the CMS.
  Generate builds it from the set name; the client check
  (`seoSlugProblem()` in `cmsFormUI.js`), `createCardPost` and
  `updateCardSet` all enforce lowercase letters, numbers and single
  hyphens. Saving a live set also fails if another live set already uses
  the slug (a query of the `blogStatus-year-index` GSI), so the build's
  duplicate check can't be tripped from the CMS.
- **No `index.html` in the address.** Each page is written as
  `reviews/<slug>/index.html` and linked as `/reviews/<slug>/`. A web
  server answers a folder URL with that folder's `index.html`, the same
  way `/` shows the root `index.html`. A spike page confirmed it on
  Amplify: the slash form returns 200, the no-slash form 301s to it, and
  `/reviews/<slug>/index.html` also works. The folder layout was chosen
  over `<slug>.html` files because Amplify would only serve those at
  `/<slug>.html`, and a clean extensionless address would need one
  rewrite rule per set in the Amplify console (not in git). The canonical
  is the slash form, so the `/index.html` duplicate is harmless.
- **Old URLs.** `waxReviews.html?...` still works (above), including
  `&setID=` links. The 2004/mcd special case still redirects to the
  lockout page. A `sortOrder=last` parameter is dropped when the address
  is rewritten. An old link with `pageName` but no `blogCat` gets its
  category from `resolveBlogCat()` (`helper.js`) and loads normally.
- **Social previews.** Facebook, Discord, Reddit and X read only the raw
  HTML, so only a slug URL gets a per-set preview; a shared old-style
  link gets the generic one.

## Where the pages physically live

Only inside the Amplify build artifact and the deployed site; not in git.
Amplify clones the repo onto a temporary build machine, the generator
writes `reviews/` and `sitemap.xml` into that checkout, Amplify zips
the whole directory and deploys it, and the machine is discarded.
`.gitignore` lists `/reviews/` and `/sitemap.xml`. To see them, fetch the
live URLs (for example `/reviews/index.json`); to get a local copy run
`node tools/generateReviewPages/generate.mjs`, which writes the same files
into the working folder (ignored by git) and also modifies the tracked
static pages it pre-renders into (discard those). Because the artifact is
the whole repo, `amplify.yml` itself is also served at `/amplify.yml`, like
`tools/` and `Documentation/` already are; only `Old HTML Pages/` is
removed before deploy (2026-11-05).

## The rest of the build: minified assets

Since 2026-10-30 the same build also minifies the public scripts and the
stylesheet. It is described here because it shares `amplify.yml` and the
"generated in the build, never committed" rule with the review pages.

**What happens.** After the generator, `node tools/minifyAssets/minify.mjs`
rewrites the build's own copies of `scripts/helper.js`, `wax.js`,
`ticker.js`, `blogs.js`, `playerSearch.js`, `browseBySet.js`,
`timeline.js`, `waxMuseum.js` and `styles/styles.css` in place, with a linked source map
(`helper.js.map` and so on, readable source embedded) beside each. The
URLs don't change and no HTML changes, so every page, including every
generated review page, picks the minified files up automatically. The repo
keeps readable source and nothing minified is committed; the build machine
is thrown away. The CMS scripts, `auth.js`, `scripts/fonts/*` (already
base64, nothing to gain), deprecated scripts and the inline `<script>`
blocks in the HTML are not touched.

**Why this way.** The site already served Brotli, so the gain is smaller
than raw sizes suggest but still about half: raw 260,043 to 135,417 bytes
across the 8 files, and over the wire about 67 KB to 34.5 KB (live:
`helper.js` 9.2 to 5.8 KB, `wax.js` 11.3 to 6.5 KB, `styles.css` 24.9 to
11.4 KB; a review page goes from about 56 KB to 28 KB, and the browser
parses less). Doing it in the build, not by committing minified copies,
means no drift between source and output, and the source stays what you
edit and read.

**The tool.** esbuild, installed by `npm ci` from a root `package.json`
and `package-lock.json` (the only dependency in the repo outside
`Lambdas/`), pinned to 0.19.12 because 0.19 is the last line that supports
the build image's Node 16. Each file is minified on its own, with no
bundling and no format option: esbuild then keeps every top-level
`function`, `let`, `const` and `var` name, which matters because inline
`onclick` handlers and calls between scripts rely on those names, and only
shortens local names. `rm -rf node_modules` runs last because the artifact
is the whole directory and would otherwise publish the installed packages;
that is also why `node_modules` isn't cached between builds (`npm ci` takes
about half a second here).

**Safety.** The tool overwrites files, so it refuses to run unless
`AWS_APP_ID` is set (Amplify sets it) or `--force-in-place` is passed;
`--root <dir>` points it at a scratch copy, which is how it was tested. It
fails the build, leaving the previous deployment live and the notifier
emailing the log, if any file is empty, not smaller, missing its source
map, or has lost a top-level name found at the start of a line in the
source (a regex check, so keep top-level declarations at the start of a
line). It must run after the generator, which reads the readable
`helper.js` and `waxReviews.html`.

**Working with it.** Edit the readable source only. A new public script or
stylesheet must be added to the list in `minify.mjs` or it ships unminified.
A production console error shows minified lines unless dev tools are open
(they fetch the `.map` and show the real file and line). The build log
prints the before and after bytes per file. `npm audit` prints a notice for
esbuild 0.19.12; it concerns esbuild's development server, which is never
run here, and moving to a newer esbuild needs a newer Node than the image
has.

**How it was verified.** On a scratch copy (generate, then minify): 46
browser checks gave identical results for the original and minified copies,
and 36 screenshots (12 pages at 1300, 768 and 390 px, with recorded API
data, a fixed random seed and fonts) were pixel-identical. On production
(build #3157): 10 pages at two widths with no console errors, links
upgraded, the checklist modal working, the `.map` files served and
`/node_modules/` returning 404.

## How static the site is now

Until 2026-11-19 the generated HTML held the metadata but not the
review. Now the review, its details, images, breadcrumbs and structured
data, and every checklist, are in the HTML, so crawlers that don't run
JavaScript see the full text and a visitor sees the review without
waiting for the API. What stays browser-only: the vote buttons and
pagination, the checklist modal on a review page, the checklist page's
filters and PDF export, and the ticker. The browser also redraws each
review from the API after load, so an edit shows up there before the
build that bakes it in has finished.

### Compared with an enterprise headless-CMS static setup

A typical enterprise setup (a headless CMS such as Contentstack feeding a
Next.js, Astro or Gatsby build) has the same shape: the CMS is the source
of truth, a publish event triggers a build, the build pulls content from a
delivery API, and static output goes to a CDN.

| Enterprise setup | This site |
|---|---|
| CMS with content types, fields and workflow | cardStack CMS plus the DynamoDB `Cards` table |
| Delivery API (token-protected, CDN-cached) | `getPublicCardSets` (public, cache header) |
| Publish webhook | DynamoDB Stream plus `cardsRebuildTrigger` |
| Framework build (Next, Astro, Gatsby) | `generate.mjs`, string replacement into one HTML file |
| Launch, Vercel or Netlify hosting | Amplify Hosting |
| Build alerts | `amplifyBuildNotifier` |

Where the enterprise version goes further:

- **Hydration.** A framework attaches its scripts to the prerendered
  markup. Here the browser redraws the review from the API instead, which
  costs one request per page view.
- **Incremental builds.** On-demand revalidation rebuilds just the changed
  page in seconds. Here every build regenerates all of the roughly 128
  pages and takes about three minutes, which is fine at this size but
  would not scale to thousands of pages.
- **Content workflow.** Versioning and rollback, scheduled publishing,
  roles, audit logs, references between entries and localisation. Here a
  set is live or staged, with no history.
- **Preview.** Live preview against a draft API and a preview deployment
  per branch. Here the CMS preview modal, which shares
  `buildCardSetMarkup()` with the live page, and no staging site.
- **Templating.** Components, typed routing, image optimisation. Here one
  HTML file with marker comments that the generator checks for.

The step this section once listed as "not planned", running
`buildCardSetMarkup()` at build time with each set's full text, is the
2026-11-19 change described under "The review, pre-rendered".

## Failure modes and safeguards

- **Generator fails** (bad data, API down during the build, template
  markers broken): build fails, previous deployment stays live, the
  notifier emails the log link. While the API is down, builds started by
  unrelated pushes fail the same way.
- **Minifier fails** (a file not smaller, a missing source map or a lost
  top-level name, or `npm ci` unable to reach the npm registry): the build
  fails the same way, the previous deployment stays live and the notifier
  emails the log. A CMS save starts a build, so until it is fixed new
  content doesn't reach the site either.
- **A checklist fails to load during the build:** after three tries the
  build fails, the same way, so no page links to a missing checklist
  page. A year's full records failing only costs its pages the
  pre-rendered review (a warning in the log).
- **Duplicate or invalid slug:** rejected at save time by the CMS Lambdas,
  so the generator's own check should never trip.
- **Build in progress or failed:** a freshly saved set's page does not
  exist for about three minutes. The links come from the manifest, so no
  link points at it before it exists. The admin page's **Review Pages
  Check** (`cms/admin.html`) requests every live set's page and lists any
  that are missing; a miss that persists means a failed build.
- **Stale static page** (a set changed but the build has not finished, or
  failed): the raw HTML (social previews, crawlers that don't run
  JavaScript) shows the old version. The page's JavaScript redraws the
  review and corrects the tags for browsers and Google. A checklist page
  has no such redraw of its text until its data loads.
- **Trigger not firing:** check `/aws/lambda/cardsRebuildTrigger` in
  CloudWatch, and `aws amplify list-jobs --app-id d20qsyoicusf3p
  --branch-name main --region us-east-2` for a recent job.

## One-time AWS setup (done 2026-10-30)

1. DynamoDB, table `Cards`, Exports and streams: turn on the stream with
   **New and old images**.
2. Lambda `cardsRebuildTrigger` (Node, source in
   `Lambdas/cardsRebuildTrigger/index.mjs`, pasted into the console). Role
   permissions: the managed policy `AWSLambdaDynamoDBExecutionRole`, plus
   an inline policy allowing `amplify:StartJob` on
   `arn:aws:amplify:us-east-2:339740904141:apps/d20qsyoicusf3p/branches/main/jobs/*`.
3. Trigger on that Lambda: the `Cards` stream, batch size 100, batch
   window 60 seconds, starting position Latest, retry attempts 3.
4. The roles of `createCardPost` and `updateCardSet` each need an inline
   policy allowing `dynamodb:Query` on
   `arn:aws:dynamodb:us-east-2:339740904141:table/Cards/index/blogStatus-year-index`
   (for the duplicate-slug check; without it every live save fails).
5. `getPublicCardSets` must be the version that returns `stars` (and,
   since 2026-11-19, `checklistUpdatedAt`).
6. Since 2026-11-19, `saveChecklist` writes `checklistUpdatedAt` on the
   `Cards` item and `cardsRebuildTrigger` watches it and the review
   fields; until both are redeployed, a checklist or review-text change
   reaches the static pages only with the next build.

## Cost

Only Amplify build minutes. A build takes about 2.4 minutes (recent jobs
142 to 193 seconds) and is billed per build minute (about $0.01 at the
time of writing; check current pricing), so roughly $0.02 to $0.03 a
build, under $1 a month at around 30 saves, and inside the 1,000 free
build minutes a month while the account is within its free tier.
Reading a DynamoDB Stream from Lambda is free, the trigger Lambda and the
duplicate-slug query are negligible, and hosting grows by about 128 small
files. The generator's API reads (37 year requests and 64 checklists per
build, about one Player Search's worth of `Checklists` reads) add about
15 seconds and negligible DynamoDB cost. There are no standing charges. The manifest also removed the
per-page-view API call an earlier design needed. Installing esbuild and
minifying add about a second to a build (the log showed `npm ci` at 0.4 s
and the minifier at 0.1 s), so the build minutes don't change.
